sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two types of covenant (bris) in divine service, using the examples of Avraham's covenant with Avimelech and the covenant of the divided pieces, and applies this to the unique covenant of Rosh Hashanah.

translations.translation: And the root of the difference between these two aspects,
it is known that regarding the matter of covenant there are two modes.
One mode is like the covenant that Avraham Avinu made with Avimelech by means of seven ewes,
that both of them participated in the ewes,
that each one had a portion in this,
and through this they become unified.
And the second mode is,
that they take one complete thing and cut it in two, and those who make the covenant pass between the pieces.
And behold,
when one cuts one thing into two, this is seemingly the opposite of wholeness and is division, etc.,
but in truth, this is the true unity,
namely that each one by itself is only half a thing,
and has no existence whatsoever without the other.
And likewise it will be understood above as well,
that the aspect of the covenant of Torah in the service of "and you shall gather in your grain," etc.,
behold, even though through this a drawing down of light is effected,
nevertheless, it is an existence unto itself.
However, the Torah that comes after the prior service of will and desire and teshuvah,
for teshuvah is also a covenant,
as it is written,
"to pass you into the covenant of Havayah your G-d,"
this is in a more elevated manner,
that it has no existence unto itself, etc.,
and through this there is a drawing down of light that is above the chain of descent.
And with this will also be understood the matter of the covenant of Rosh Hashanah,
as it is written,
"You are standing today, etc., to pass you into the covenant,"
for seemingly it is not understood,
behold, also throughout the year there is a covenant of Ein Sof and Yisrael,
and what is the matter of the covenant of Rosh Hashanah?
But the explanation is,
that the covenant of the entire year is in the manner of the covenant of the seven ewes,
however on Rosh Hashanah it is the service of teshuvah,
which has no existence unto itself, etc.,
and it is the unity in Ein Sof Himself, the Master of Will.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains Rashi's commentary on "Eikev" as referring to light commandments, connecting it to the concept of Yaakov (yud-eikev) and the service of will and desire that elevates one above intellect, making all commandments equal.

translations.translation: And with this will also be understood what Rashi explained on the verse "And it shall be, because (eikev) you will hearken,"
"if the light commandments that a person treads upon with his heel (eikev) you will hearken."
And this matter is as stated in the Zohar
on the verse,
"Why should I fear in days of evil, the iniquity of my heels surrounds me,"
which is the matter of the light transgressions that a person treads upon with his heel.
For behold,
regarding Yaakov it is written,
"and his hand was grasping the heel of Esav,"
for Yaakov means yud-eikev,
that he illuminates in all levels until the aspect of the heels,
and this is the matter of vigilance in all matters,
even in the lightest of the light,
and this is yud-eikev.
And the root of the drawing down of Yaakov—yud-eikev,
that there should be in him vigilance even in the lightest of the light,
is as it is written,
"the voice is the voice of Yaakov,"
"the first voice is deficient and the latter voice is full,"
"the latter voice that is full is the Torah,"
"and the first voice that is deficient is the voice that is not heard,"
and this is the matter of the service of will and desire.
And when "the voice is the voice,"
the first voice and the latter voice,
and it is the Torah that comes after the service of will and desire,
then there exists the matter of Yaakov,
yud-eikev,
which is the matter of vigilance even in the lightest of the light.
That is to say, when his service is according to reason and intellect,
then there is a distinction between the lightest of the light and the most severe of the severe,
but when he has the drawing down of Torah after the prior service of will and desire, which is above reason and intellect,
then there is no distinction at all between light and severe,
and this is "the voice is the voice of Yaakov,"
and when "the voice is the voice of Yaakov," then "the hands are not the hands of Esav" that rule.
And this is what is said: "Why should I fear in days of evil, the iniquity of my heels surrounds me,"
because the aspect of Yaakov—yud-eikev—is lacking,
and "his hand was grasping," etc.
And this is what Rashi explained on the verse "And it shall be, because (eikev) you will hearken,"
"if the light commandments that a person treads upon with his heels,"
because this verse explains the matter of the drawing down that is above the chain of descent,
which is through the Torah that comes after the prior service of will and desire,
and therefore Rashi explained that there must be vigilance even in light commandments,
for this is an indication that his service is above reason and intellect, therefore he is vigilant in the light as in the severe.
And since his service is above reason and intellect,
then "Havayah your G-d will keep for you the covenant and the kindness and the oath,"
that the light that is above the chain of descent will be drawn down.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section describes the two modes in service—prayer and Torah—as corresponding to night and day, the heart, soul, and might, and Written and Oral Torah, which will ultimately reveal the hidden lights of shoham and yashfeh in the future.

translations.translation: And behold, these two modes in service,
the service of "the voice is the voice,"
prayer and Torah,
are the service that is in the manner of from below upward and in the manner of from above downward,
as is explained at length in many places.
And since in holiness there is inclusion and unification,
behold, also in the service of prayer itself
there exist these two modes,
the service of night and the service of day.
And it can be said that in this manner is also the distinction between the service of "with all your heart and with all your soul" and the service of "with all your might,"
and also within the service of "with all your might" there exist these two modes,
for "with all your might" includes the aspect of will and the aspect of delight.
And likewise in Torah itself
there exist these two modes,
and they are the Written Torah and the Oral Torah,
as explained elsewhere.
And through these two modes in our service during the time of the duration of the exile,
in the future there will be the two modes of shoham and yashfeh.
For now, in the time of exile, it is in concealment,
for both the ascent that is made in the world and the drawing down of light in the world are in concealment,
and in the future that which they effected through service in the time of exile will be revealed,
"and I will make your windows of kadkod, and your gates of kadkod, and all your borders of precious stones,"
and it will be like this and like that.
